q: Match the grammar type to its machine: Type 1 (context-sensitive) corresponds to…
explain: Type 0 goes with Turing machines, type 1 with LBAs, type 2 with PDAs, and type 3 with finite automata.

q: Which is the correct order of strict inclusions?
explain: Each level of the Chomsky hierarchy strictly contains the one below it.

q: In the Chomsky hierarchy, what is the highest-numbered (most restrictive) type that {aⁿbⁿcⁿ | n ≥ 1} belongs to?
explain: It is not context-free (topic 17), but a noncontracting grammar generates it (topic 19).

q: What does a universal Turing machine U take as input?
options: An encoding ⟨M, w⟩ of a TM M together with an input w
explain: U reads the description of M and simulates M on w. The stored-program computer is built on the same idea.

q: HALT = {⟨M, w⟩ : M halts on w} is…
explain: Simulating M on w recognises HALT: accept if the simulation stops. But the diagonal argument shows that no TM decides it.

q: In the diagonal proof, D(⟨M⟩) does the opposite of what H predicts about M on ⟨M⟩. Running D on ⟨D⟩ shows that…
options: D halts on ⟨D⟩ exactly when it does not, so H cannot exist
D never halts, so H exists
explain: Feeding the machine its own description creates the contradiction. The only assumption made was that H exists, so H cannot exist.

q: Because the halting problem is undecidable, no program can ever determine whether any specific program halts.
explain: False. Many specific programs can be analysed. What is impossible is a single algorithm that is correct for every program and input.

q: To prove a new problem P undecidable using reductions, you show that…
options: a decider for P could be used to build a decider for HALT (or A<sub>TM</sub>)
a decider for HALT could solve P
explain: You reduce from the known undecidable problem to P. If P were decidable, HALT would be too, which is impossible.

q: Which problems about Turing machines are undecidable?
options: Does M have more than 10 states?
explain: The first three are properties of the language L(M), and Rice's theorem makes each of them undecidable. The number of states can simply be read from ⟨M⟩.

options: A → aB, A → a, A → ε (or the left-linear forms)
A → γ, for any string γ
explain: Regular grammars are right-linear (or left-linear). The other rule forms belong to types 2, 1 and 0.
